observations.behavior: Removes a session-level execution time limit for warehouse materialization queries.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces the maximum runtime of Trino-backed warehouse ingestion or model-building queries. This could allow longer-running warehouse operations to complete without being forcibly terminated by this client-side cap.

observations.behavior: Removes a 30-second metadata statement timeout for alias reconciliation in warehouses.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows metadata statements during warehouse alias management to exceed their previous strict 30-second ceiling, potentially supporting more complex warehouse schemas or slower metadata responses.

observations.behavior: Updates test assertions after removing the explicit SET SESSION command; no longer checks that the first execute call was setting the run-time limit.
observations.posthog_connection: Supportive change reflecting removal of the configuration; does not independently establish benefit but preserves compatibility with the removed behavior.

observations.limitations: The documentation hunk P1.F4.H1 and P1.F5.H1 remove an upper bound on warehouse query duration. While this removes a potential failure mode, it also increases exposure to resource exhaustion if underlying warehouse performance is poor. No tests demonstrate recovery from long-running failures or account for increased cost risk. The tier remains bounded because the implementation only removes a guard rather than adding broader safeguards or systemic improvements.

review.reason: Changes are substantive: they remove client-side execution time caps for warehouse operations, which could prevent premature termination of legitimate long queries while still remaining localized to warehouse ingestion and aliasing paths. This fits tier 2 as a bounded capability improvement without demonstrated systemic reach or comprehensive validation.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to PostHog's warehouse connectors and managed warehouse offerings where Trino-backed materialization and model building occur. Removing these limits may help complete warehouse-dependent workflows that previously failed due to short timeouts.
review.uncertainty: Documentation changes do not prove runtime behavior; no test assertions verify improved completion rates or absence of incidents. Tier assignment relies solely on removal of explicit bounds.
